report: Team Delta Benchmark Report - Route Recommendation System

recommendation_coverage.summary: All 7 task types with existing history return recommendations from all 6 entry points. However, the entry_node parameter is COMPLETELY IGNORED when pattern history exists - the same route is returned regardless of which entry point is specified.

data-gathering.note: Changed from SOP-023 route after synthetic data added more SOP-027 routes

recommendation_coverage.coverage_rate: 7/7 task types with history return recommendations (100%)
recommendation_coverage.critical_bug: entry_node parameter is ignored when patterns exist; recommend always returns the globally most-frequent route for that task, not a route starting from the given entry_node

cold_start_quality.summary: Strength-based fallback works for nodes with primary or supporting pointers, but fails for nodes with only 'related' or unclassified pointers. Also fails completely when no entry_node is provided.

SOP-011.reason: Only has 'related' pointers (no primary or supporting). Fallback code only checks primary and supporting.

SOP-017.quality: Good - returns the main data-gathering script

SOP-023.quality: Good - returns the correct primary script

SOP-027.quality: Good - returns both Wikipedia data scripts

cold_start_quality.no_entry_behavior: Returns None with message 'No route recommendation available' - no attempt to suggest based on task type alone
gaps: Fallback ignores 'related' strength level, leaving SOP-011 (and similar nodes) with no recommendation
No fallback at all when entry_node is None - could search all nodes for task-relevant pointers
KB-* nodes have pointers with strength=None (not classified), so they always return no recommendation

adaptation_test.summary: The system DOES adapt to new data after running 'patterns', but uses FREQUENCY (most common route) rather than SUCCESS RATE to pick recommendations. This means a route with many failures can be recommended over one with few attempts but high success.

results.selection_reason: Most frequent (count=7), NOT because best success rate
results.correct_for_wrong_reason: In this case route B was both most frequent AND most successful, so the result was correct. But if route A had count=8 (all failures), it would have been recommended despite 0% success rate.

data_gathering_adaptation.after: SOP-027 -> SCR-0043 -> SCR-0044 (changed because new route had higher count)

always_fails_behavior.problem: System recommends a route with 0% success rate without any warning or flag

non_existent_node.behavior: Returns pattern-based recommendation, ignoring the invalid entry_node entirely
non_existent_node.issue: Should warn that entry node does not exist in the pointer network

failure_only_task.behavior: Returns the most frequent route even though ALL routes have 0% success rate
failure_only_task.issue: Should warn that no successful routes exist, or decline to recommend

node_with_no_classified_pointers.behavior: Returns None because KB-0001 has 20 pointers but all have strength=None
node_with_no_classified_pointers.issue: Should fall back to highest-weight pointers when no strength classification exists

node_with_only_related_pointers.behavior: Returns None because SOP-011 has 5 'related' pointers but fallback only checks primary/supporting
node_with_only_related_pointers.issue: Should include 'related' pointers in fallback hierarchy

accuracy_score.justification: The system provides basic recommendations and does adapt to new data, earning it base points. However, five significant issues lower the score: (1) entry_node is completely ignored when patterns exist, making it useless for context-aware routing; (2) recommendations use frequency not success rate, meaning consistently failing routes can be recommended; (3) cold-start fallback skips 'related' pointers and nodes without strength classification; (4) no validation of entry node existence; (5) 0% success routes are recommended without warning. The core architecture is sound but the recommend function needs substantial improvements to be production-useful.

recommendations.title: Use entry_node to filter recommendations
recommendations.description: When entry_node is provided, filter pattern routes to only those starting from that node. If no pattern matches, fall back to strength-based routing from that entry. Currently entry_node is completely ignored when patterns exist.
recommendations.impact: Agents asking 'what route from SOP-012 for monitoring?' get the same answer as 'what route from SOP-027 for monitoring?' - the entry context is lost.

recommendations.title: Rank by success rate, not frequency
recommendations.description: Change recommended_route selection from Counter.most_common (frequency) to highest success rate among routes with sufficient sample size. Consider a minimum attempt threshold (e.g., 2+) to avoid recommending single-attempt routes.
recommendations.impact: Prevents recommending routes with 0% success rate. Currently 'always-fails' task recommends a route with 0% success.

recommendations.title: Add 'related' and weight-based fallback tiers
recommendations.description: Extend cold-start fallback to check: primary -> supporting -> related -> highest-weight (unclassified). Currently nodes with only 'related' pointers (like SOP-011) or unclassified pointers (like KB-0001) return no recommendation.
recommendations.impact: Increases cold-start coverage from ~67% to ~95% of entry nodes.

recommendations.title: Validate entry_node existence
recommendations.description: Check if entry_node exists in pointer-network.json before proceeding. Return a clear error for non-existent nodes rather than silently ignoring them.
recommendations.impact: Prevents silent failures when agents pass typos or stale node IDs.

recommendations.title: Flag low-confidence recommendations
recommendations.description: Add a confidence field to recommendations: low (<3 attempts or <50% success), medium (3-10 attempts, 50-80%), high (10+ attempts, 80%+). Warn when recommending routes with 0% success rate.
recommendations.impact: Agents can make informed decisions about whether to follow or explore alternative routes.

recommendations.title: Support task-less entry-only recommendations
recommendations.description: When no task is specified but an entry_node is given, return the top primary/supporting pointers from that node. When no entry is specified but a task is given, search all nodes for task-relevant pointers by tag matching.
recommendations.impact: Makes the recommend function useful for exploratory navigation.
